2027-06-08.title: Tuesday of the third week after Pentecost · St Mariam Thresia
readings: A person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ
The Spirit of truth will testify on my behalf; you also are to testify
2027-06-08.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Third Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Mariam Thresia (1876–1926), virgin, of Puthenchira, foundress of the Congregation of the Holy Family.
2027-06-08.verse: You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning.
theo: The Epistle today takes us into one of the sharpest moments of the early Church. At Antioch, Peter had been eating with Gentile believers, and then, when visitors came from Jerusalem, he drew back, as if the table of Christ had two classes of guests. Paul opposed him to his face, and in today's verses he gives the reason: “We ourselves are Jews by birth and not Gentile sinners; yet we know that a person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ. And we have come to believe in Christ Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in Christ, and not by doing the works of the law, because no one will be justified by the works of the law.” Paul is not speaking against good works, nor against the law God gave to Israel. He is saying that no one, Jew or Gentile, can stand before God by a record of achievements. We are made righteous because Christ has loved us and given himself for us, and we receive that gift by faith. That is why the table cannot be divided: everyone who sits there sits by the same grace. In the Holy Qurbono the priest and the newest catechumen, the old family and the migrant worker, come forward with the same empty hands.

Then Paul adds a warning: “But if I build up again the very things that I once tore down, then I demonstrate that I am a transgressor.” He means the walls that Christ pulled down between people, and the old self-reliance that grace pulled down in us. It is possible to be set right by God and then quietly to begin building again: to start keeping accounts of our virtues, to look down on those who pray less or give less, to think that our place at the altar is earned. The Christian life is not a building of our own that God inspects at the end; it is a life received. St Augustine put his whole experience of grace into one short prayer: give what you command, and then command what you will (Confessions 10.29, in substance). Everything good we do is first his gift, and our part is to receive it and not to block it.

The Gospel comes from the Last Supper. Jesus promises: “When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who comes from the Father, he will testify on my behalf. You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning.” There are two witnesses here, the Spirit and the disciples, and they speak together. The Spirit does not testify instead of us; he testifies through us, in our words and our lives. Today the Church remembers one in whom that double witness was very plain: St Mariam Thresia of Puthenchira, near Thrissur. Born in 1876, she gave herself from childhood to prayer, and as a young woman she went with a few companions to the homes of the sick, the dying and the poor, and to families torn by quarrels and debts, without asking which church or which community they belonged to. In 1914 she founded the Congregation of the Holy Family to carry on this work, and she died on 8 June 1926. Pope Francis canonized her on 13 October 2019. She was a daughter of the Syro-Malabar Church, and our Panchangam keeps her memory with gladness, for the saints belong to the whole Church. Her works were many, but she never thought she had earned anything by them: she was simply letting the Spirit testify to Jesus through her hands. In this month when families settle into a new school year and the monsoon keeps people indoors, she reminds us that the first place of witness is the home.
outline: Ask: do I live as someone who has received everything, or as someone who is building up a record?
Point 1 · Justified through faith in Jesus Christ
No one stands before God by achievements; the same grace seats all at one table.
Point 2 · Do not build again what grace tore down
The walls between people and the pride of self-reliance.
Point 3 · The Spirit testifies, and you also
St Mariam Thresia: a witness carried into the homes of the poor and the sick.
“You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning.”
live: Begin each good work today with a short prayer: Lord, this is your gift; let me not spoil it.
Visit, or at least telephone, one family you know that is going through sickness, debt or a quarrel, and pray with them if they wish.
2027-06-08.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you loved us and gave yourself for us, and by faith in you we are made righteous before the Father. Keep us from building again the walls you have pulled down and the pride you have broken in us. Send us the Spirit of truth, who comes from the Father, to testify to you in our words and our lives. Through the prayers of St Mariam Thresia, who carried your love into the homes of the sick, the poor and the troubled, make our families holy, peaceful and open to all who need us. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar no one is seated by merit: the Body and Blood of Christ are given to sinners made righteous by his love, and from the altar we are sent, like St Mariam Thresia, to carry that love from house to house.
conn: Galatians 2:11–14, just before today's reading, tells how Paul opposed Peter when Peter drew back from eating with Gentile believers; today's verses give the principle behind the dispute: all are justified by faith in Christ.

John 15:26–27 promises the Spirit's testimony and the disciples' testimony together; Acts 1:8 shows the promise fulfilled when the Spirit comes and the apostles become witnesses to the ends of the earth.
St Mariam Thresia gave her congregation the name of the Holy Family of Nazareth (Luke 2:51–52), and she sent her sisters into homes as the Spirit's witnesses.
fathers: Give what you command, and command what you will: every good work is first God's gift before it is ours (Confessions 10.29, in substance).
When Paul writes “who loved me and gave himself for me”, he teaches each believer to say it personally, as if Christ had died for that one person alone (Commentary on Galatians 2:20, in substance).
magis: The grace of the Holy Spirit has the power to justify us, cleansing us from our sins and giving us the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ and through Baptism (in substance).
The Christian family is a specific revelation and realization of the communion of the Church, and for this reason it can and should be called a domestic church.
The moral life of Christians is sustained by the gifts of the Holy Spirit, permanent dispositions that make us docile in following his promptings.

quick: Paul teaches that a person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ.
Jesus promises the Spirit of truth, who will testify to him, and he tells the disciples that they also must testify.
St Mariam Thresia (1876–1926) of Puthenchira carried that witness into the homes of the poor and the sick and founded the Congregation of the Holy Family.
2027-06-08.action: Do one hidden act of kindness for a family in need today, and thank God for the grace to do it.
2027-06-08.question: Do I quietly count my good works, as if they earned me my place before God?

family.explain: Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit, who tells the world about him. Then Jesus said: you too will tell about me. Today we remember St Mariam Thresia, who lived in Kerala about a hundred years ago. She went from house to house with her friends to help sick people, poor people and families who were fighting. She did not make speeches; her kindness told people about Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for families in our neighbourhood who are sick, poor or unhappy, that someone may bring them the love of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Which family near us needs our help, and what small thing can we do for them this week?”

illus: A retired schoolteacher in Thrissur district told her grandchildren how, as a small girl, she had been very ill with fever during a monsoon, when her father was away and her mother was alone with four children. Late one evening two sisters in plain habits came up the muddy path with a lantern, a little rice and some medicine. They sat with her through the night so that her mother could sleep. Years later she learned that they belonged to the congregation founded by Mariam Thresia. She said: they never told us anything about Jesus that night, but from then on I knew what he was like. Stories of this kind are told in many Kerala homes; this one is an example of the witness the Spirit gives through ordinary hands.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, Spirit of truth. Testify to Jesus in us, and through the prayers of St Mariam Thresia make our homes places of peace and our hands ready to serve. Amen.
share: A person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:16). Where do I still try to earn God's love?
He will testify on my behalf. You also are to testify (John 15:26–27). How has someone's life testified to Jesus for me?
St Mariam Thresia went into the homes of the sick and the troubled. Which home is God asking me to enter with his love?
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may be one table where all are welcomed by the same grace.
For the Congregation of the Holy Family and all religious who serve families, the sick and the poor.
For families broken by quarrels, debts, addiction or illness, that they may find peace and healing.
For those who have grown proud of their own goodness, that they may rediscover the joy of grace.
For our parish, that the Holy Spirit may testify to Jesus through our homes.
pm.close: Father, you justify us through faith in your Son and you send your Spirit to testify to him in us. Through the prayers of St Mariam Thresia, keep us humble before your grace and generous in serving families in need. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: A name the Second Vatican Council and the Catechism give to the Christian family (Lumen Gentium 11; Catechism 1656–1657, 2204). In the home the faith is first proclaimed, prayer is learned and love is practised; the family is the Church in miniature. St Mariam Thresia devoted her life and her congregation to the holiness of families.
kidsaint: St Mariam Thresia and the lantern path

When Mariam Thresia was a young woman in Puthenchira, she and her friends went out to visit people who were very sick, even at night, carrying lamps along the village paths. They washed the sick, cooked for them, prayed with them, and stayed with the dying so that no one would die alone. Some people laughed at her, but she kept going because she saw Jesus in every sick person. Lesson: when we help someone who is weak, we are helping Jesus himself.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul says today: we know that a person is justified not by the works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:16). That is good news for every one of us. We do not stand before God with a list of our achievements. We stand before him because Christ loved us and gave himself for us.

Paul also warns us: if I build up again the very things that I once tore down, then I demonstrate that I am a transgressor (Galatians 2:18). Grace pulled down our pride and the walls between us. Let us not build them up again by counting our good deeds or looking down on others.

In the Gospel Jesus promises the Holy Spirit: he will testify on my behalf. You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning (John 15:26–27). The Spirit speaks, and we speak; the Spirit works, and we work. Today we remember St Mariam Thresia of Puthenchira. She went into the homes of the sick, the poor and the troubled, and the Spirit testified to Jesus through her hands.

So let us receive God's grace with humility, and let us carry it into homes, beginning with our own. A visit, a meal, a prayer at a sickbed, a quarrel healed: this is how the Spirit testifies today. Amen.
kids: Children, do we have to earn God's love by being very good? No! God loves us first, and Jesus gave his life for us. That is a gift. Because we have received it, we want to share it. Today we remember St Mariam Thresia from Kerala. She loved Jesus so much that she went to visit sick people and poor families, and helped them. When you help your mother at home, or share with a friend who has nothing, you are telling people about Jesus without even using words.

intro: Theme: “You also are to testify because you have been with me from the beginning.”
On Tuesday of the third week after Pentecost, the memory of St Mariam Thresia: justified by faith, not building again what grace tore down, and the witness of the Spirit through our hands.

points.h: Justified through faith in Jesus Christ
sub: No one stands before God on a record of achievements.
The same grace seats everyone at one table.
Good works flow from grace; they do not buy it.
q: but the righteous live by their faith.
For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God
points.apply: Begin your prayer each morning this week by thanking God for one gift you did nothing to earn.

points.h: The Spirit testifies, and you also
sub: The Spirit works through our words and hands.
Witness begins with being with Jesus.
q: You are my witnesses, says the Lord, and my servant whom I have chosen
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses
points.apply: Spend ten minutes with Jesus before the tabernacle or with the Gospel before you try to speak of him to anyone.

points.h: St Mariam Thresia: faith working through love
sub: A girl of Puthenchira given to prayer.
From house to house: the sick, the poor, the quarrelling.
The family as the domestic church.
q: Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
the only thing that counts is faith working through love.
points.apply: Choose one family, your own or a neighbour's, and do one concrete thing this week to bring it peace.

concl: We are made righteous by grace, not by our record, and grace makes us witnesses.
The Spirit who testified to Jesus through St Mariam Thresia wants to testify through our homes and our hands.
2027-06-08.resolve: Receive everything as gift, and let the Spirit carry Christ's love through you into one home this week.
